title: SAML session provisioning grace window and adaptive MFA step-up policy
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Goal: Define and ship a robust session management policy for SAML/SSO that balances smooth JIT provisioning with strong step-up (MFA) rules for privileged actions, improves logout propagation, and enhances audit logging for session events.

Background: We currently accept IdP assertions and create user accounts via JIT provisioning with a long-lived session cookie. This has led to inconsistent MFA expectations for users who are provisioned with default roles, and inconsistent logout/reauth behavior when admins revoke access or when an IdP-initiated logout occurs. We also need richer audit events (session creation, reauth, MFA step-up, logout propagation, admin revocation) for compliance and incident investigation.

Scope: This ticket covers the policy and implementation plan for: (1) a configurable provisioning grace window for newly JIT-provisioned users before full role bindings and step-up rules apply, (2) adaptive MFA step-up triggers tied to RBAC v2 privileged roles and sensitive console actions, (3) reliable SA/IdP-initiated logout propagation and session revocation hooks, and (4) additional audit log schema for session lifecycle events. Implementation will include runtime checks in the auth gateway, Console admin controls to force sign-out, and migration of session metadata into the audit event stream.
acceptance_criteria: Configurable JIT provisioning grace window exists (default 24h) and is stored per-organization; values can be set via Admin Console and org-level config API
Users provisioned within the grace window inherit minimal default roles; role bindings requiring explicit approval or higher sensitivity enforce MFA/step-up before performing sensitive actions
MFA step-up rules are evaluated at request time for RBAC v2 actions labeled 'sensitive' and for any user with roles above 'developer', with the policy configurable per-org and overridable by admins

SP-initiated and IdP-initiated logout produce reliable session revocation across all active nodes; revoked sessions cannot be used for API or console access within 1s of revocation under normal operating conditions

Audit log schema includes structured events: session.created, session.jit_provisioned, session.stepup.required, session.stepup.completed, session.revoked, session.logout.propagated; events include actor, reason, auth_method, idp_assertion_id, session_id, and role_snapshot
Admin Console exposes a per-user 'force sign-out' and 'view active sessions' UI; actions are recorded in audit logs and visible in retention-backed logs
No performance regression >2% on auth gateway median latency under standard load after changes (validated by load test), and staging rollout completes without new flaky failures
Security review completed and documented in the ticket; rollout plan and rollback path validated with SRE and Compliance
implementation_notes: Auth gateway changes: add session metadata flags (provisioned_at, provision_grace_expires, role_snapshot) to JWT/session store and evaluate step-up at policy decision point
Console: admin page for org config (provisioning grace window, step-up policy thresholds) + per-user session list + force sign-out button that calls revoke endpoint
Auth API: new endpoints for bulk session revocation and session introspection for audits; ensure endpoints are rate-limited and RBAC protected
Audit pipeline: extend event schema, add enrichment with idp_assertion_id and role_snapshot, ensure events land in longterm storage (30d by default) and are queryable via Console and ELK/Datadog
MFA signalling: prefer SAML assertion attribute (e.g., authn_ctx or custom 'acr') when present; otherwise evaluate local state and identity provider assurance level mapping
Migration: backfill provisioned_at for existing users using first_seen timestamp; default existing users to grace_expires = provisioned_at + 0 (i.e., no grace) unless org opts-in
Testing: unit tests for policy evaluation, integration tests with Okta and AD FS test tenants for IdP-initiated logout, e2e test for force sign-out across nodes
Rollout: feature-flagged rollout per-org with metric dashboards (session_revocations, stepup_prompts, auth_gateway_latency) and canary to 5% of orgs before global rollout

risk_and_mitigation: Risk: Too-aggressive grace window may allow privilege escalation if default roles are powerful. Mitigation: default minimal role, require explicit approval for privileged roles and require MFA step-up for role elevation.

Risk: Logout propagation delays under network partitions. Mitigation: use event-sourced revocation with idempotent revocation tokens and local short-lived cache invalidation; SRE will monitor and tune time-to-revoke metrics.
Risk: Audit volume spike. Mitigation: sample non-critical session events for orgs under quota; critical events always recorded. Provide org-level retention controls.

Risk: Breaking SAML integrations that do not provide authn context. Mitigation: map legacy IdP assert to lowest-assurance level and prompt step-up based on action; document compatibility notes in SSO onboarding docs.
